To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

lower levels of serum albumin, higher neutrophil to Lymphocyte ratio, higher levels of inter-dialysis weight gain, decrease of pre-dialysis systolic pressure and increase of NLR over time are associated to increased mortality hazard rate.

the mortality risk for ESRD patients on hemodialys is related to the levels of albumin and neutrophil to lympocyte ratio at the beginning of treatment, as well as the change in predialysis blood pressure, and neutrophil and lymphocyte counts over time.

lower levels of predialysis albumin, higher interdialytic weights, higher neutrophil to lympocyte ratio, and lower predialysis systole blood pressure at the beginning of follow-up time are associated with increased hazard rates of mortality, as well as increase of neutrophils to lymphocyte ratios over time.
